hints.content: **Reflective (or line) symmetry** means that we can reflect a figure across a line, and the figure will remain unchanged.

##Reflection over $y=4$

Under this transformation, some points on the triangle map to another point which is no longer on the triangle. The triangle is *not symmetric* over this line.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A right triangle mapped onto a coordinate plane. The x- y-coordinate plane scales by ones. The right triangle has a point at four, zero, a point at three, seven, and a point at seven, four. The equation y equals four is graphed on the coordinate plane. Dotted lines show the locations of the points after the right triangles is reflected over the graphed line. The image points are outside the current pre-image.

hints.content:
##Reflection over $y=\dfrac{1}{7}x+3$

This line goes through one of the corner points, $(7,4)$, and the midpoint of the opposite side of the triangle. 

Under this transformation, each point on the triangle maps to another point which is also on the triangle. The triangle is *symmetric* over this line.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A right triangle mapped onto a coordinate plane. The x- y-coordinate plane scales by ones. The right triangle has a point at four, zero, a point at three, seven, and a point at seven, four. The equation y equals one over seven x plus three is graphed on the coordinate plane. Dotted lines show the locations of the points after the right triangles is reflected over the graphed line. The image points are mapped on the current pre-image.

hints.content:
The symmetries that apply to the triangle are:

Symmetry | Applies to the figure?
:- | :-:
Reflective symmetry over the line $y=4$ | No
Reflective symmetry over the line $y=\dfrac17x+3$ | Yes
